title: Eleven things independent Indian makers sell that you didn't know existed
excerpt: Bidri, Longpi, dhokra, ittar, palm-leaf etching. Things made by hand in India that never reach a search box, and how to buy any of them without getting it wrong.
seoTitle: 11 Indian Crafts You Didn't Know Existed
seoDescription: Bidri ware, Channapatna, Longpi pottery, dhokra, kantha, ittar and more — handmade things from India most people never discover, and how to buy them well.

title: Kundan, polki, jadau, meenakari: what the words actually mean
excerpt: Three of them are methods and one is a stone. Two pieces described identically can differ in price twentyfold. The differences, and the four questions that settle it.
seoTitle: Kundan vs Polki vs Jadau vs Meenakari Explained
seoDescription: Polki is uncut diamond, kundan is a setting technique, jadau is the whole craft and meenakari is enamel on the back. What each means and how to check.

title: How to buy silver in India (and why yours probably isn't hallmarked)
excerpt: Silver hallmarking is voluntary in India, which puts the checking on you. Sterling against plated, what German silver really is, and the one mistake that ruins oxidised pieces.
seoTitle: Buying Silver Jewellery in India: A Guide
seoDescription: Silver hallmarking is voluntary in India. What 925 and 999 mean, how to spot plated silver, why German silver has none, and how to care for oxidised pieces.
seoKeywords: how to buy silver jewellery india

title: Temple jewellery: the oldest design language still being worn
excerpt: Made for deities first and dancers second, which is why the relief is deep and the stones read from thirty feet. The forms, the three price tiers, and how to spot cast from hand-raised.
seoTitle: Temple Jewellery: Forms, Materials and Buying
seoDescription: Vanki, oddiyanam, jhumka and manga malai explained, what kemp stones are, the three material tiers sold as temple jewellery, and how to tell cast from repoussé.

title: Handloom or powerloom: six ways to tell, in your hands
excerpt: The two look identical in a photograph and differ severalfold in price. The selvedge, the reverse, the light test — checks you can do standing in a shop.
seoTitle: Handloom vs Powerloom: How to Tell the Difference
seoDescription: Six physical checks that separate handloom from powerloom cloth — selvedge pinholes, the reverse, thread density against light — and what GI tags don't prove.

title: Block print or screen print: how to spot the difference before you pay
excerpt: A block print has a heartbeat — registration drift where the block landed a hair off. Five tells, the regional styles, and what to expect in the first three washes.
seoTitle: Block Print vs Screen Print: How to Tell
seoDescription: Five ways to identify hand block printing — registration drift, the join line, ink texture, the reverse and colour count — plus Bagru, Sanganer and Ajrakh.
seoKeywords: hand block print vs screen print

title: Six Indian weaves worth knowing by name
excerpt: Chanderi, Maheshwari, Kota Doria, Jamdani, ikat, Kanjeevaram — what each is for, which climate it suits, and why weight decides more of your wearing than beauty does.
seoTitle: Six Indian Weaves Worth Knowing by Name
seoDescription: Chanderi, Maheshwari, Kota Doria, Jamdani, ikat and Kanjeevaram — how to recognise each, what climate it suits, what to check, and how to store them.

title: Brass, bronze, copper: which one, for what, and the patina question
excerpt: Three metals sold interchangeably that behave completely differently around food. The acid rule, what German silver really is, and whether to polish or let it go.
seoTitle: Brass vs Bronze vs Copper: A Buyer's Guide
seoDescription: Which metal is safe for water, cooking and eating, why acidic food and bare copper alloys don't mix, and whether to polish brass or keep the patina.

title: Terracotta, stoneware, porcelain: what survives an Indian kitchen
excerpt: Firing temperature decides everything — whether a piece holds water, takes a flame or survives a dishwasher. How to read the unglazed foot, and what throwing rings tell you.
seoTitle: Terracotta vs Stoneware vs Porcelain Explained
seoDescription: How firing temperature decides porosity and flame safety, how to identify each from the unglazed foot, and how to spot wheel-thrown from slip-cast.

title: Lacquered wood: Channapatna, Etikoppaka, and toys that outlive childhood
excerpt: The colour is fused into the wood by friction, not painted on, which is why it wears thin instead of flaking. What to look for, and the three things that damage it.
seoDescription: How lac is fused onto turned wood by friction, why Channapatna toys are safe for children, and how to tell real lacquerware from moulded imitations.

title: What "handmade" is allowed to mean
excerpt: The word is unregulated, which makes "is this handmade?" the wrong question. Five better ones, what variation should look like, and how to spot a reseller.
seoDescription: Handmade is an unregulated claim. The spectrum from hand-made to hand-packed, five questions better than asking if it is handmade, and spotting a reseller.

title: Gifting without guessing
excerpt: Most gift-buying goes wrong when you stop thinking about the person and start thinking about the occasion. Six categories that reliably land, and what to avoid.
seoTitle: How to Choose a Gift That Actually Lands
seoDescription: Questions that reveal what someone will actually use, six handmade gift categories that reliably work, and the logistics people forget until too late.
